name: playwright
summary: Microsoft Playwright MCP: browser automation by a local headless browser, no credentials

connect.identity: <none: runs a local browser, no account>
connect.description: Playwright MCP (local stdio, headless isolated browser)

notes: No credentials: this server needs no account or key.

Needs Node.js 18 or newer (the package's engines field and the README agree). Browsers must be installed for Playwright before first use; the README's own 'Browser installation' section is empty, so install them with Playwright's standard install step and check the result.
Pinned to @playwright/mcp@0.0.83 (the npm latest on 2026-10-14); the README itself suggests @latest, which this template deliberately avoids. Update the pin on purpose.

Safety flags chosen here: --headless (the default is a visible window), --isolated (profile kept in memory, nothing saved to disk) and --block-service-workers. Files outside the workspace roots and file:// URLs are blocked by default; do NOT add --allow-unrestricted-file-access.

Do not add --no-sandbox: it disables the browser sandbox for every process type. Also avoid --extension (drives your real Chrome or Edge with its logins), --user-data-dir (persistent profile), --cdp-endpoint, --secrets and --caps unless you need them.

--allowed-origins (semicolon-separated) and --blocked-origins narrow what the browser requests, but the README says they do not affect redirects and are not a security boundary; the README also says Playwright MCP is not a security boundary. Page content is untrusted, so pages can try to steer the model.
--allowed-hosts is a different thing: the hosts this server may serve from (only relevant to the HTTP transport, not stdio).

Policy: asks first before navigating to a page, running page scripts (browser_evaluate, browser_run_code_unsafe), uploading files, saving files and touching cookies or storage. Note that most useful work involves browser_navigate, so expect a prompt per navigation.
No smoke test is set: the only read-only tool without navigation is browser_tabs, whose action argument values are not spelled out in the README.
